calls.reason: Builder.ai's insolvency and SimpleClosure's limited sample do not establish a broad customer downturn or link it to falling provider revenue and greater dependence on big tech.

HandRefiner and Sora documentation establish rendering errors and structural difficulties. They do not establish Zitron's broader causal explanation that models lack knowledge; the evidence supports only part of the claim.
The Guardian and CNN reporting link automated curation to false and garbled stories. But describing MSN as destroyed is an undefined editorial judgment, which those incidents cannot settle.
Schwab and Kiplinger document an October selloff involving AI financing concerns and other pressures. They do not establish the sweeping industry damage predicted in this undated statement of belief.
Synergy measures the three firms' combined cloud market share at 67%. That does not show whether nearly every AI purchase sends some revenue to them through direct or indirect payments.

OpenAI identifies Azure as its exclusive cloud provider, and Google says Claude runs on Google Cloud. These hosting arrangements support the ordinary reading that serving interactions contributes to big-tech infrastructure revenue.
